Consonantal i

Clothes & getting dressed

cotton noun and adjective

classical

M-O s.v. cloth, types: cotton
Plin. NH 19.14: fruticem, quem aliquī gossypion vocant, plūrēs xylon

1gossypium: Latin ending -um (Pliny’s Greek form gossypion). Plin. NH 19.14. Neither gossypium nor gossypinus is a headword in the local Lewis & Short.

gossypium1, gossypiī n.

noun, second declension

Traupman has no word for cotton.

Examples

  • Ex quō facta est haec tunicula? — Ex gossypiō.

    What is this T-shirt made of? — Cotton.composed

Other words

  • gossypinus, gossypina, gossypinum — of cotton

    also used · modern · M-O, citing Pliny

  • xylina — cotton cloth

    also used · classical · Plin. NH 19.14

See also linen, wool, cloth, T-shirt.

SourcesLewis & Short: gossypion · Lewis & Short: xylon

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. cloth, types: cotton.
